text:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: multiple TLS handshake failures detected for api-prod in us-east-1. Error rate spiked at 02:12 UTC. If you are oncall, please acknowledge and join #incidents.

rob: acked. I'm oncall and looking. Seeing lots of `ERR_SSL_PROTOCOL_ERROR` and `TLS handshake timeout` in the edge logs. Rolling up.

alisa: noted, I'm joining. Are we seeing 5xx spikes upstream or TCP resets?

rob: mostly client-side failures. Edge logs show `short read` during ClientHello for a subset of flows. Per-region alarm: us-east-1 primary.

mike: grabbing tcpdumps now on the fronting LB (haproxy) and one of the backend proxies. `tcpdump -i any host 10.4.2.12 and port 443 -w /tmp/tls-conn.pcap`

kyle: I see the cert-rotation job ran at 02:11:53 UTC (cert-operator). Could be related. But that alone shouldn't cause mass ClientHello failure unless chain mismatch or partial rollout.

rob: good flag. Mike, any handshake traces?

mike: attaching a snip of `openssl s_client` against the IP:
```
$ openssl s_client -connect 10.4.2.12:443 -servername api.redwood.com -tls1_2 -msg -state
CONNECTED(00000003)
>>> TLS 1.2 Handshake [length 0090], ClientHello
<<< ??? [length 0000]
read:errno=104
```
No ServerHello returned when run from inside the AZ for some clients.

alisa: that's weird. Packet capture shows ClientHello leaving, but no server response in many flows. I notice PMTU is ~1500 for some paths and ~9000 for others.

netops: FYI we applied a BGP/MTU change to one transit peer around 02:08 UTC to stabilize jumbo frames. Could be related. We rolled back the BGP change at 02:30 but by then impact happened.

rob: hypothesis 1: PMTU/MTU mismatch causing fragmented ClientHello or ICMP blackhole — server never receives full ClientHello, so no ServerHello. Hypothesis 2: cert rotation produced partial chain and some proxies reject handshake. Let's triage in-thread.

mike: evidence for PMTU: tcpdump on haproxy shows multiple TCP segments where initial ClientHello length is 1750 bytes and gets fragmented. I also see no ICMP frag-needed.

kyle: evidence for cert rotation issue: logs from cert-operator: `INFO pushed cert api.redwood.com new=2026-03-14T02:11:53Z` but not all proxies reported success; some returned 503 on health checks around same time.

rob: ok split tasks: Mike & Netops - validate MTU/PMTU and check if ICMP is being filtered. Alisa & Kyle - validate cert chain across proxies and check HA config for partial rollout. I'll coordinate customer comms with csm_liz.

csm_liz: prepping a short customer note /internal/summary for affected tenants. Will update once we have impact numbers.

mike: results: on haproxy host `ip link show eth0` -> `mtu 1500`. Backend proxy has `mtu 9000` on its ENI. I can reproduce handshake fail from a client VM that uses path with 1500 MTU -> server expects 9000 -> fragmentation happens and path doesn't send frag-needed back (ICMP filtered by transit).

mike: tcpdump snippet (hex omitted) shows ClientHello split across two TCP segments; server ACKs first segment but does not respond to the split ClientHello.

netops: checking transit ACLs, we do have ICMP type 3/code 4 filtered on one of the peering fabric boxes (policy applied accidentally during a change window at 02:05). That would hide PMTU changes and cause TCIP/TLS blackholes.

alisa: that aligns. For the cert side, I validated the certificate chain served by a failing proxy using `openssl s_client -connect <ip>:443 -servername api.redwood.com -showcerts` and it serves the new cert and intermediates correctly. No obvious chain mismatch.

kyle: addl logs: haproxy on some frontends had `SSL handshake: error:1408F10B:SSL routines:ssl3_get_record:wrong version number` for a minority of flows but that looks like the outcome of truncated ClientHello rather than cert issue.

rob: ruling: primary cause is PMTU blackhole introduced by the peering ACL change; cert rotation coincided but wasn't root cause. Chain: 02:05 change -> 02:11 cert rotation started -> 02:12 client errors spike due to fragmented ClientHello lacking ICMP feedback -> 02:32 mitigation applied.

kyle: mitigations applied: 1) Netops re-enabled ICMP frag-needed on the transit peer at 02:30 UTC. 2) Temporarily reduced MTU on backend proxies to 1400 to avoid fragmentation at 02:31. 3) Restarted haproxy worker processes to clear stuck sockets in a few hosts at 02:35. 4) Added fallback routing to us-east-2 for heavy customers at 02:40 (manual traffic drift).

mike: after MTU set to 1400 and ICMP allowed, `openssl s_client` completes handshake consistently.

csm_liz: customer impact summary draft: ~22 minutes of elevated TLS handshake failures in us-east-1 (02:12–02:34). Error rate hit ~11% of requests for the hosted API path. Affected customers: 6 mid-market tenants saw degraded API request success rates; no data exfiltration. Will send customer-facing note in 15 min.

oncall-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident acknowledged by rob, severity set to sev2, start_ts=2091123456.

pagerduty-bot: @rob handoff reminder: next oncall is alisa at 03:05 UTC.

rob: handing off to alisa now. All current mitigations in place. If anything changes, flag here.

alisa: thanks. I'm taking ownership for post-incident RCA and action items.

rob: outgoing note: summary + timeline to include in RCA.

rob: TIMELINE (working):
- 02:05 UTC: Transit ACL change applied (accidental ICMP frag-needed block)
- 02:11:53 UTC: cert-operator rotates certs for api.redwood.com across fleet (normal job)
- 02:12 UTC: Spike in TLS handshake failures observed at edge; customers report errors
- 02:20 UTC: Initial triage indicates fragmented ClientHello and missing ICMP responses
- 02:30 UTC: Netops rollback ACL allowing ICMP frag-needed; MTU mitigation started
- 02:31–02:35 UTC: MTU reduced to 1400 on affected proxies; haproxy workers restarted
- 02:40 UTC: Traffic partly shifted to us-east-2 as fallback for heavy customers
- 02:45 UTC: Error rates back to baseline for most customers
- 03:05 UTC: Oncall handoff from rob -> alisa

kyle: ACTION ITEMS (initial):
- netops: postmortem of ACL change process and add safety guard rails (owner: netops).
- infra/edge: implement pre-rotation TLS synthetic check that verifies handshake over typical MTU paths (owner: kyle).
- infra: ensure cert-operator has rollout health checks that validate reachability for large ClientHello sizes (owner: alisa).
- product/security: add monitoring for sudden PMTU/fragmentation patterns in edge metrics and alert (owner: mike).

netops: noted and will produce a timeline for the ACL change and patch the change process. We'll also whitelist ICMP frag-needed temporarily across peering until health-check gating is in place.

alisa: tagging follow-ups into the RCA doc. Will assign owners and due dates. First pass RCA will be delivered EOD.

csm_liz: sent customer note to affected tenants summarizing impact and mitigations; will attach postmortem link when available.

rob: thanks everyone. Quick wins: add explicit PMTU check to our canary test, and for now make cert-rotation jobs gate on a quick handshake probe via an alternate path.

mike: additional diagnostic logs I've saved to /var/log/incidents/2091123456/tls-pcap.tar.gz and uploaded to infra-s3 at s3://redwood-incidents/2091123456/tls-pcap.tar.gz

oncall-bot: :tada: Incident status: mitigated. severity=sev2, end_ts=2091125634.

alisa: I'm taking this to RCA; assigning myself as owner. Will ping once the draft is ready.

rob: handoff complete. :thumbsup:
